payload.prompt:
You are starting a coding agent session from structured task context and evidence.

Scope model:
- The "active task" is Inputs.task (the single task object included below).
- Only plan and execute work required to complete the active task.
- All other provided entities (designDoc, plan, initiative, adjacentScopeTasks, evidenceItems) are context and scope constraints only.
- Any additional tasks present in evidenceItems are provided for context and scoping only, never as implementation targets.
- Implementing functionality whose primary outcome belongs to any non-active task is a hard failure and will be rejected.

Your primary goals:
1. Build a concrete multi-step execution plan.
2. Surface discrepancies between provided inputs and this session's in-repo delivery reality.
3. Ask clarification questions only when they block safe execution.
4. Keep the execution plan scoped to the current task and treat adjacentScopeTasks as out-of-scope boundaries.

Inputs:
{
  "task": {
    "id": "72274bf3-51df-4707-9830-294e497601c7",
    "title": "Create plan-document refinement and approval UI",
    "description": "Build a UI workflow that enables users to view the generated plan document, make inline refinements, request changes through conversational interaction, and ultimately approve the document before it's persisted and featured on the plan page. The workflow supports iterative refinement where users can edit content directly or ask the system to revise sections, with clear approval gates before the document becomes the official plan.",
    "details": "Create a multi-step UI workflow with the following components:

1. **Plan Document Viewer**: Display the generated plan document with:

- Readable narrative sections (user journey, technical implementation)
- Mermaid charts
- Clear visual hierarchy showing connections between user journey and technical implementation
- Responsive layout suitable for both desktop and tablet viewing

2. **Inline Editing**: Enable users to:

- Click and edit text sections directly (narrative, descriptions, ownership)
- Add or remove sections
- Preserve formatting and chart positioning during edits
- Show edit history or change indicators

3. **Conversational Refinement**: User standard Hey Hey conversation side-panel:

- Request changes to specific sections ("regenerate the sequence diagram", "expand the technical implementation narrative")
- Ask clarifying questions about the plan
- Provide feedback that the LLM uses to refine the document
- Maintain conversation context across multiple refinement round

5. **Approval Gate**: Implement clear approval workflow:

- "Request Changes" button that opens conversational refinement panel
- "Approve" button that locks the document and persists it
- Optional approval checklist (e.g., "All stages assigned?", "Timing realistic?")
- Confirmation dialog before final approval

6. **Integration with Plan Page**: Upon approval:

- Persist the plan document to the system
- Feature it prominently on the plan page
- Link plan document to the associated initiative and plan
- Make document accessible for future reference and updates",
    "acceptanceCriteria": "- Users can view the generated plan document with all sections (user journey, technical implementation) and embedded charts (sequence diagrams, system diagrams) rendered correctly
- Users can click and edit text content inline (narrative, descriptions, ownership) without losing formatting or chart positioning
- Users can request changes through conversational side-panel and see the document update based on refinement requests within 30 seconds
- At least two rounds of refinement can be completed before approval without losing previous edits
- Change tracking or version history shows what was modified and allows reverting to previous versions
- Approval workflow includes clear "Request Changes" and "Approve" buttons with optional approval checklist validating key plan properties
- Upon approval, the plan document is persisted and appears on the plan page within 5 seconds
- UI provides clear visual feedback when document is locked (approved) and cannot be further edited
- Error handling gracefully manages failed refinement requests, chart re-rendering, or persistence failures
- Responsive design works on desktop (1920px+) and tablet (768px+) viewports"
  },
  "plan": {

    "title": "Create plan-document refinement and approval UI"
  },

Name: Create conversational planning workflow (nodes & transitions)
Status: COMPLETED
Priority: MEDIUM
Sections:
- description: Define and implement the conversational plan-intake flow that guides users through the Implementation Plans planning phase. This workflow will surface gaps in work (tasks, design documents, services) through iterative dialogue, align with the plan-document schema and sequencing template, and establish the foundation for structured plan generation. The workflow should follow the Planning intake conversation requirements and mirror the architectural patterns established in the onboarding flow.
- details: Implement a conversational workflow using the same flow architecture as the onboarding workflow, with eight core nodes that guide users through iterative planning. The workflow begins with a welcome and outcome clarification, then systematically discovers scope, constraints, and dependencies through targeted questions. The DISCOVER_GAPS node cycles through three distinct categories—tasks scattered across initiatives, design documents, and services—surfacing missing work that would otherwise remain fragmented.

As gaps emerge, the workflow transitions to PROPOSE_STAGES, which presents high-level execution phases aligned with the plan data model (stages represent major milestones or phases). For each proposed stage, the PROPOSE_STEPS node surfaces specific work items (tasks, design documents, services) that belong to that stage, allowing users to refine sequencing, ownership, and timing. This two-level proposal pattern mirrors the plan schema structure and enables users to think about work both strategically (stages) and tactically (steps within each stage). Users can cycle through gap discovery and proposal multiple times, returning to DISCOVER_SCOPE for additional context or revisiting PROPOSE_STAGES and PROPOSE_STEPS for refinements.

The workflow leverages context transforms to accumulate discovered gaps and proposed entities across conversation turns, progressively building the plan-document schema as dialogue evolves. Conditional routing adapts based on plan complexity and user confidence, ensuring the conversation remains focused and efficient. The workflow maintains references to related initiatives, existing tasks, and services throughout, grounding recommendations in organizational context. Upon completion, the onComplete behavior triggers plan-document generation with all identified work sequenced by stage and step, ownership assigned, and dependencies established. The generated plan artifact becomes the single source of truth—navigable and immediately usable by the execution guidance system.
- acceptanceCriteria: - Workflow includes minimum 8 nodes covering welcome, outcome clarification, scope discovery, gap discovery (3+ types), stage proposal, step proposal per stage, refinement, plan generation, and completion
- Transitions enable looping for iterative discovery and refinement without requiring user to restart
- Context transforms accumulate and structure gap discoveries and proposed entities in alignment with plan-document schema
- Workflow successfully surfaces at least 3 distinct types of gaps (tasks, design docs, services) in a single planning session
- PROPOSE_STAGES node presents high-level execution phases aligned with plan data model; PROPOSE_STEPS node surfaces specific work items per stage as stubs (name and short description only)
- Two-level proposal pattern (stages then steps) enables strategic and tactical refinement with sequencing, ownership, and timing adjustments; step stubs defer detailed refinement to post-planning phase
- onComplete behavior generates a plan document with all identified work sequenced by stage and step, ownership assigned, and dependencies established
- Plan document is created in a format that aligns with the plan-document schema and sequencing template
- Workflow code follows the same architectural patterns as the onboarding flow (node definitions, transitions object, contextTransforms, onComplete)
- Workflow is integrated with the plan-document generation system so users receive a complete, navigable plan artifact upon completion"

      "content": "TASK a1a0c2a3-a441-4741-9eec-578301314678
Name: Add UI for Gap discovery
Status: COMPLETED
Priority: MEDIUM
Sections:
- description: Build a UI component that guides users through gap discovery in a structured, progressive sequence. After the conversational planning phase (where scope and constraints are established), the system presents identified gaps in three stages: services first (highest-level, easiest to validate), then design documents (mid-level implementation patterns), then tasks (detailed work items). Each stage is presented one at a time, allowing users to confirm or refine selections before moving to the next category. This progressive disclosure prevents cognitive overload, gives users a chance to contribute their own knowledge of existing work, and provides the system with richer context for subsequent stages—especially for task discovery, where knowing the selected services and design docs enables more precise recommendations.
- details: The UI implements a three-stage gap discovery flow that runs after the conversational planning phase concludes, with analysis performed once and results cached for efficient retrieval. Stage 1 presents identified services with a simple validation interface: the system shows services it inferred from the scope discussion, the user confirms which are in scope, and optionally adds missing ones. Once services are locked in, Stage 2 presents design documents relevant to those services—again with confirmation and optional additions. Stage 3 then presents tasks, now informed by both service and design doc selections, allowing the system to surface more precise and contextual work items.

Each stage uses a card-based or list interface showing the entity name, brief description, and relevance reasoning (why the system thinks it belongs in this plan). The user can toggle items on/off, add new ones via a search or creation flow, and must confirm the current stage before advancing to the next—no skipping or backtracking allowed. A progress indicator shows which stage is active and how many stages remain. This progressive disclosure prevents cognitive overload, gives users a chance to contribute their own knowledge of existing work, and provides the system with richer context for subsequent stages. By the time the user reaches task discovery, the system has explicit confirmation of services and design docs, enabling it to filter and prioritize task recommendations more effectively.

The system distinguishes visually between system-identified and user-added entities, ensuring transparency about the source of each recommendation. Once all three stages are confirmed, the UI triggers generation of the structured plan document with sequencing, ownership, and timing. This approach balances speed (analysis happens once) with UX clarity (results presented one category at a time) and information richness (each stage informs the next).
- acceptanceCriteria: - UI presents gap discovery in three sequential stages (services → design docs → tasks) with clear visual progress indicator
- Each stage shows system-identified entities with relevance reasoning and allows user to confirm, reject, or add items before advancing
- User cannot proceed to next stage until current stage is confirmed (no skipping or backtracking)
- Gap analysis is performed once after planning phase concludes; results are cached and retrieved by each stage rather than re-analyzing
- Task discovery stage receives service and design doc selections as context and surfaces only tasks relevant to confirmed selections
- User can add new entities (services, design docs, tasks) within each stage via search or creation flow
- UI clearly distinguishes system-identified entities from user-added entities through visual indicators
- Confirmation of all three stages triggers generation of the structured plan document with sequencing, ownership, and timing"
    },
    {
      "id": "ccf0631b-002c-4eda-9a7f-30d73798766b",
      "type": "task",
      "title": "Build stage drill-down UI for step details",
      "content": "TASK ccf0631b-002c-4eda-9a7f-30d73798766b
Name: Build stage drill-down UI for step details
Status: COMPLETED
Priority: MEDIUM
Sections:
- description: Implement the drill-down interface that allows users to expand a stage and view all steps within it, including ownership, timing, and dependencies. This enables tactical refinement at the step level and provides detailed visibility into the work contained within each stage.
- details: Create a drill-down interface component that displays detailed step information for a selected stage. When a user selects or expands a stage from the stages visualization, this component should render a list or table of all steps within that stage. For each step, display: step name, description, assigned owner(s), estimated timing/duration, actual timing (if in progress or completed), dependencies (both internal to the plan and external), status (not started/in progress/completed), and any relevant metadata from the plan-document schema. The component should support inline editing or interaction for refinement of ownership, timing, and sequencing. Include visual indicators showing step status and dependency relationships. Support sorting and filtering of steps by status, owner, or timing. Provide navigation back to the stages view. Consider how this component integrates with the next steps quick-view component to avoid duplication. The drill-down should maintain context about which stage is being viewed and enable comparison with other stages if needed.
- acceptanceCriteria: - Drill-down component displays all steps for selected stage from plan-document schema
- Each step displays name, description, owner, estimated timing, status, and dependencies
- Step status indicators clearly show not started/in progress/completed states
- Dependencies are visualized and indicate both internal and external relationships
- Component supports sorting by status, owner, and timing
- Component supports filtering to show only specific step statuses
- Users can navigate back to stages view while maintaining plan context
- Component integrates with plan-document schema and renders data correctly
- Inline editing or interaction for ownership and timing refinement is functional
- Visual design is consistent with stages visualization component and overall application design
- Accessibility requirements met: semantic HTML, ARIA labels, keyboard navigation, screen reader compatibility
- Component handles edge cases: stages with no steps, steps with multiple owners, circular dependencies"
    },
    {
      "id": "a5a03b19-95ec-4e38-b5f5-920a9963f548",
      "type": "task",
      "title": "Integrate plan UI with plan-document schema",
      "content": "TASK a5a03b19-95ec-4e38-b5f5-920a9963f548
Name: Integrate plan UI with plan-document schema
Status: COMPLETED
Priority: MEDIUM
Sections:
- description: Connect the UI components (stages, steps, next steps) to the plan-document data model so they render correctly from the structured plan artifact. Ensure all data flows properly from the conversational workflow output to the UI layer, establishing the plan document as the single source of truth for visualization.
- details: Implement data integration layer that connects the three plan UI components (stages visualization, step drill-down, next steps quick-view) to the plan-document schema. This involves: (1) Creating data mappers that transform plan-document schema output from the conversational workflow into the format expected by each UI component; (2) Establishing reactive data bindings so UI components update when plan-document data changes; (3) Implementing plan-document loading and caching logic; (4) Creating dependency resolution logic that the next steps component can use to determine which steps are unblocked; (5) Ensuring all three components reference the same underlying plan-document instance to maintain consistency; (6) Adding error handling for malformed or incomplete plan documents; (7) Implementing serialization/deserialization logic if plan documents are persisted. Assume the plan-document schema is defined in the 'Design plan-document schema and sequencing template' task. The integration should follow existing application architecture patterns for data management. Include comprehensive logging for debugging data flow issues.
- acceptanceCriteria: - All three UI components (stages, steps, next steps) correctly render data from plan-document schema
- Data mappers transform plan-document output into format required by each UI component
- Reactive bindings ensure UI updates when plan-document changes
- Plan documents load correctly and are cached appropriately for performance
- Dependency resolution logic correctly identifies unblocked steps
- All three components reference same plan-document instance (no data inconsistency)
- Error handling gracefully manages malformed or incomplete plan documents
- All data flows from conversational workflow output through integration layer to UI
- Plan document serves as single source of truth for all UI rendering
- Integration follows established application architecture patterns
- Comprehensive logging enables debugging of data flow issues
- Performance: UI components render within 500ms of plan-document data availability
- Integration tested with plan documents of varying complexity (5 stages, 50+ steps; single stage, 1-2 steps)
- No data loss or corruption during serialization/deserialization cycles"
    },

Return a strict JSON object with this exact structure and lowerCamel keys:
{
  "responseType": "startup_plan_v1",
  "sessionTitle": "short, task-focused session title",
  "executionPlan": [
    {
      "stepId": "step-1",
      "title": "short title",
      "description": "what to do",
      "references": [
        {
          "sourceType": "evidenceItem|task|designDoc|plan|initiative",
          "sourceId": "entity or evidence id",
          "rationale": "why this source supports this step"
        }
      ],
      "validationFocus": "what the user should verify before implementation"
    }
  ],
  "discrepancies": [
    {
      "sourceRef": {
        "sourceType": "evidenceItem|task|designDoc|plan|initiative",
        "sourceId": "entity or evidence id"
      },
      "sourceField": "title|content|topologySummary|description|details|acceptanceCriteria|sections.<sectionKey>|outcome|adjacentScopeTasks.<index>.description|adjacentScopeTasks.<index>.acceptanceCriteria",
      "sourceExcerpt": "one or two full sentences from input",
      "reasoning": "one or two sentences explaining the mismatch",
      "discrepancyText": "one or two sentence concise discrepancy statement",
      "severity": "low|medium|high"
    }
  ],
  "clarificationQuestions": [
    {
      "question": "blocking question text that is not already captured in discrepancies",
      "reason": "why this blocks safe execution and is not already covered by a discrepancy",
      "relatedSourceRefs": [
        {
          "sourceType": "evidenceItem|task|designDoc|plan|initiative",
          "sourceId": "entity or evidence id"
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}

Rules:
- sessionTitle must be specific to the active task and concise (prefer 3-8 words).
- sessionTitle must not be generic (for example avoid "Startup Plan" or "Task Work").
- Every discrepancy must include a precise sourceRef and sourceField.
- In startup-plan format, discrepancy means a mismatch between provided inputs and what is required to deliver Inputs.task in this codebase/session.
- Do not emit fragmentary excerpts; sourceExcerpt must be one or two full sentences.
- Every executionPlan step should include at least one reference when possible.
- Treat Inputs.task as the only implementation target for this session.
- Treat designDoc/plan/initiative/evidenceItems as contextual guidance and scope evidence, not separate implementation targets.
- Treat additional tasks included in evidence as strict out-of-scope boundaries for implementation in this session.
- Treat adjacentScopeTasks as boundary constraints, not additional work for this session.
- Do not include executionPlan steps whose primary outcome belongs to an adjacentScopeTask.
- Do not include executionPlan steps whose primary outcome belongs to any task other than Inputs.task.
- If Inputs.task includes work that is intentionally split across services/repositories, treat this as an allowable scope split and plan only the subset deliverable in this codebase/session.
- Do not treat allowable scope splits (for example, task details that mention backend storage or API behavior during a ui-common-scoped session) as contradictions that block planning.
- Work that is intentionally implemented in another repository/service is not, by itself, a discrepancy for this startup plan.
- Record a discrepancy for cross-repository state only when it directly conflicts with or blocks this session's acceptance criteria.
- If you record an allowable scope split as a discrepancy, keep severity low unless it directly blocks Inputs.task acceptance criteria for this session.
- If progress is blocked by adjacent-scope dependencies, capture that as a discrepancy or clarificationQuestion instead of planning adjacent-scope implementation.
- If an issue is already listed in discrepancies, do not repeat it in clarificationQuestions.
- Use clarificationQuestions only for unresolved blockers that are not already represented as discrepancies.
- Prefer a reasonable assumption plus a low-severity discrepancy over a clarification question when safe execution remains possible.
- Do not offer follow-up implementation on any non-active task (including adjacentScopeTasks or additional tasks found in evidence).
- Prefer the smallest viable plan that satisfies current-task acceptance criteria without preemptive neighboring-task work.
- If there are no discrepancies, return an empty discrepancies array.
- If there are no blocking questions, return an empty clarificationQuestions array.


Return JSON only. Do not include markdown fences.
Do not include additional commentary outside JSON.

Okay, so we need to do a few things here. So we have the data coming back from the agent. And what we're going to get is a entityID. This will be a designDocID. It will be of a BRAINSTORM type. So I know the tasks mentioned being able to edit it and having a side by side conversation panel. For the first pass, we can skip that.

## Completion Signaling
When implementation is complete, include the exact marker "[[HEY_HEY_IMPLEMENTATION_DONE]]" in your assistant response.
